About Dhanush

I'm Dhanush Mohanasundaram, a B.E. Electronics & Communication Engineering student at Velalar College of Engineering and Technology (CGPA 8.4/10), building toward a career as a Software Development Engineer.

My focus is backend development and core engineering — Java, Python, data structures and algorithms, and system design fundamentals — sharpened through daily coding practice and hands-on projects.

I completed an AI internship at Edu-versity, exploring machine learning and Python-based workflows, and took ideas to the inter-college evaluation stage at Smart India Hackathon 2024 & 2025. As an executive member of IEEE COMSOC, I stay active in the technical community.

I'm a continuous learner with a strong problem-solving drive — laying software foundations today, moving into AI and machine learning next, and aiming to build technology that makes a real-world difference.

01

RFID Rabies Vaccination Tracking System

ReactNode.jsExpressFirebaseESP32 / RFIDView Repository ↗
Problem

Clinics struggle to track multi-dose rabies vaccination schedules and reliably follow up with each patient.

Solution

A hospital dashboard where RFID hardware (ESP32 + RC522 + fingerprint sensor) logs scans to Firebase in real time, with a React + Vite dashboard and a secured Node/Express API managing patient profiles, the Day 0–3–7–14–28 dose timeline, and automated email/SMS reminders.

Impact

A complete end-to-end system spanning hardware, backend, and frontend — with live updates, JWT auth, analytics charts, and auto-generated certificate emails on course completion.

Lessons Learned

Designing a resilient hardware → cloud → dashboard pipeline taught me to keep data contracts simple and backward-compatible with legacy records.

Technical Highlights

ESP32 microcontroller reads RC522 RFID tags and fingerprint sensor data, serialises to JSON, and POSTs to Firebase Realtime Database via HTTPS. A Node.js/Express REST API manages the Day 0–3–7–14–28 dose schedule, issues JWT-authenticated requests, and triggers email and SMS reminders. The React + Vite dashboard subscribes to Firebase streams for live updates and renders analytics charts.

02

AI-Powered Train Traffic Control

PythonAIOptimizationSIH 2025
Problem

Railway networks face scheduling conflicts that limit throughput and cause cascading delays.

Solution

A Smart India Hackathon 2025 prototype using AI-assisted decision-making and optimization to maximize railway throughput and reduce scheduling conflicts.

Impact

Selected at the inter-college idea-evaluation stage of SIH 2025; built end-to-end problem analysis and an initial solution workflow.

Lessons Learned

System-level thinking and framing a real-world transportation problem matter as much as the algorithm itself.

AI Methodology

The railway network is modelled as a directed graph where nodes are stations and edges carry capacity constraints. A constraint-satisfaction pass identifies scheduling conflicts, then a greedy-with-backtracking algorithm resolves them by deferring lower-priority trains. The SIH 2025 submission demonstrated throughput improvement via simulation on synthetic timetable datasets.

03

Road Damage Detection

PythonStreamlitComputer VisionJavaScriptView Repository ↗
Problem

Spotting and reporting road damage manually is slow, subjective, and hard to scale.

Solution

A Streamlit web application that analyses road imagery for damage through an interactive browser interface, pairing a Python backend with a lightweight web UI.

Impact

A deployable, browser-based tool that makes road-damage detection accessible without any specialized software.

Lessons Learned

Wrapping a model in a clean Streamlit interface is one of the fastest ways to make ML usable for real people.

Computer Vision Pipeline

Road images are uploaded through a Streamlit file-uploader widget. The Python backend converts images to NumPy arrays, applies edge-detection and morphological operations via OpenCV, and classifies damage severity into three tiers based on contour area thresholds. Results are overlaid on the original image and returned to the Streamlit UI for instant visual feedback.

04

Innovative Passenger Tracking System

System DesignPublic TransportSIH 2024
Problem

Public transportation lacks clear passenger visibility and monitoring, making operations harder to manage.

Solution

A Smart India Hackathon 2024 prototype and concept design to improve passenger tracking and monitoring, with a structured solution workflow and architecture.

Impact

Selected at the inter-college idea-evaluation stage of SIH 2024 through strong problem identification and ideation.

Lessons Learned

Collaborative ideation and clear solution architecture turn a rough idea into something buildable.

System Design Scope

The SIH 2024 problem required a scalable architecture for real-time passenger count monitoring across public transit. The proposed design used IoT sensors at boarding/alighting doors feeding a cloud aggregator, with a fleet-management dashboard showing occupancy heat maps per route. The evaluation validated the problem framing, technical feasibility, and data pipeline architecture.
